planting.note: Set divisions out after the last frost so plants are well rooted before cold weather returns in fall.

directions: One of the earliest releases from the University of Minnesota's cold-hardy chrysanthemum breeding program, this 1966 introduction bears small, tightly quilled pompon-form flowers in a deep rose-pink that open in early autumn. Its compact, mounding habit and northern-bred constitution let it survive winters that kill off typical florist pot mums left in the garden. Pinch new growth through June to encourage a dense, well-branched mound, and divide clumps every two to three years to maintain vigor.
sources: University of Minnesota chrysanthemum breeding program

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring to allow a full season of root establishment before the first hard freeze.

directions: Released from the University of Minnesota's chrysanthemum breeding program in 1972, Minnwhite carries clean white double flowers over a low, rounded mound of foliage. It was selected specifically for the ability to overwinter reliably in cold-climate gardens rather than being treated as an annual pot mum. Pinch stems in late spring to encourage branching, and divide every few springs to keep the clump from thinning in the center.
sources: University of Minnesota chrysanthemum breeding program

planting.note: Install divisions in spring; roots need a full growing season to establish enough cold hardiness for winter survival.

directions: A 1972 companion release to Minnwhite from the University of Minnesota program, Minnyellow produces lemon-yellow double blooms on a compact, cold-hardy mound. Both were bred to survive outdoors through harsh northern winters rather than being discarded after a single fall display. Pinch growing tips through late spring for a fuller mound, and divide congested clumps every two to three years in early spring.
sources: University of Minnesota chrysanthemum breeding program

planting.note: Set out divisions in spring so the cold-hardy root system is established before autumn bloom and winter dormancy.

directions: Introduced in 1974 by the University of Minnesota's chrysanthemum breeding program, Minnruby bears richly saturated ruby-red double flowers over a dense, low mound of foliage. Like its Minn-series siblings, it was bred for garden persistence through cold northern winters rather than for greenhouse or disposable pot-mum use. Pinch stems through late spring to build a compact habit, and divide every two to three years to renew vigor.
sources: University of Minnesota chrysanthemum breeding program

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring; the dome-shaped cushion habit needs a full season to fill out before fall bloom.

directions: Released in 1977 by the University of Minnesota's chrysanthemum breeding program, Minngopher is associated with the discovery of the now-ubiquitous cushion growth habit, in which a dome of foliage becomes almost completely covered in small maroon-red double flowers. That naturally rounded, self-branching form influenced the modern garden mum industry, which had previously relied on older, looser upright habits. Deadhead spent blooms to tidy the mound, and divide clumps every two to three years in spring.
sources: University of Minnesota chrysanthemum breeding program

planting.note: Install divisions in spring to give the cushion-habit mound a full season to establish before autumn bloom.

directions: Following on the heels of the cushion-habit breakthrough, this 1979 University of Minnesota introduction forms a tidy dome of foliage smothered in bright rose-pink double blooms each fall. Like other Minn-series mums, it was bred specifically for cold-climate garden survival rather than single-season pot display. Deadhead through the bloom period and divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring to keep plants vigorous.
sources: University of Minnesota chrysanthemum breeding program

planting.note: Set out divisions in spring; cushion-type mums need a full growing season to form their dome shape before fall bloom.

directions: A later University of Minnesota cushion-mum release from 1988, Lemonsota carries bright lemon-yellow double flowers over a compact, rounded mound bred for reliable overwintering in cold northern gardens. It extends the Minn-series line of hardy garden mums developed to replace disposable florist pot mums with true garden perennials. Pinch tips through early summer to encourage dense branching, and divide clumps every two to three years in spring.
sources: University of Minnesota chrysanthemum breeding program

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring so the cushion mound is well established before autumn flowering and winter dormancy.

directions: Introduced in 1989 from the University of Minnesota's cold-hardy chrysanthemum program, Snowsota bears white double flowers warmed by a soft cream center over a dense cushion-form mound. It continues the Minn-series breeding goal of garden mums that return reliably after harsh winters rather than needing annual replacement. Deadhead spent flowers for a tidy appearance and divide every two to three years in spring to maintain a full, healthy mound.
sources: University of Minnesota chrysanthemum breeding program
